description: A copy of data that is expensive to fetch, kept where it is cheap to read, such as memory.
A hit finds a fresh value in the cache; a miss must fetch it from the slower source.
`hits / (hits + misses)`, also called the hit rate: the share of lookups the cache answers without touching the source.
Callers ask only the cache, and the cache calls a loader on a miss and stores the result.
How long a cached value is served before the next read loads a fresh copy; it bounds the staleness.
Deleting a cached key when the source changed, so the next read loads the new value.
The database or service that owns the data; the cache can always be rebuilt from it.
